data.name: Navodit
data.gender_notes: Navodit is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Navodit is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Navodita', which means 'New' or 'Innovative'. This name is often given to a baby as a symbol of delight and hope for a new beginning. The name Navodit carries the meaning “New, Innovative, Delightful” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Navodit usually hope their child will grow to embody new, innovative, delightful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: May your life be filled with new opportunities and innovations, leading to spiritual growth and enlightenment.
data.etymology: Navodit belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “New, Innovative, Delightful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Navodit total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Navodit was a 16th century Jain monk and philosopher. He was the founder of the Navaswami Sect of Jainism. His works include 'Navaswamistotra', 'Navaswami-Prashna' and 'Navaswami-Vritti'. In his teachings, he emphasized the importance of the inner light, or Jina, in the pursuit of spiritual growth.
historical_references.context: Jain monk and philosopher, founder of Navaswami Sect of Jainism

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Navodit is found in the 'Harshcharitra' by Kalhana. He mentions Navodit as a 'bhagavat' or devotee of Vishnu, who was a contemporary of the great king Harshavardhana. Navodit is known to have composed hymns in praise of Vishnu, which are included in various Sanskrit texts.
